dedupe_keys.name: drone remote controller rf signal dataset

description: North Carolina State University researchers provide RF recordings from 17 drone remote controllers made by eight manufacturers. The controllers transmit in the 2.4 GHz band while the drones remain idle. A passive surveillance setup combines a high-frequency oscilloscope, directional grid antenna and low-noise power amplifier. Approximately 1,000 recordings per controller each span 0.25 milliseconds. The registered description identifies machine-learning and neural-network training for controller detection and classification. AERPAW also explicitly identifies interference analysis, supporting evaluation of wireless signal discrimination under the stated experimental conditions. IEEE DataPort hosts the release under CC BY 4.0. The registered issue date is 25 November 2020; the AERPAW page labels the experiment 2019, without establishing exact acquisition dates. File format, sampling rate and geographic test location are not stated in the metadata reviewed. Direct DataPort access requirements and charges could not be verified because the landing route was unavailable to the metadata browser. Limitations include the selected controllers and idle-drone condition; these recordings do not establish field coverage or general network performance. No directly related active dataset was confirmed.
